## Learning Objectives {.unnumbered}

{{< include ../learning_objectives/0645-containers-renv.qmd >}}

## Download the images before you start {.unnumbered}

The examples in this chapter build on `rocker/r-ver:4.6.2`,
which takes more than a gigabyte of disk space.
Start Docker first (on macOS and Windows, open Docker Desktop),
then download (pull) it before you start:

```bash
docker pull rocker/r-ver:4.6.2
```

## The project

This chapter puts the R packages of a small renv project into a Docker image.
It is an renv project like the ones in [Virtual environments: R (renv)](0560-virtual-environments-r-renv.qmd),
and its files are in the book repository's `demos/docker-renv/end` folder.
`hello.R` prints a message with the [cowsay](https://cran.r-project.org/package=cowsay) package:

```{.r}
cowsay::say("Hello from R in my image!")
```

`DESCRIPTION` lists the package with an exact version,
and `renv/settings.json` makes snapshots explicit,
so `renv::snapshot()` records only what `DESCRIPTION` lists, and what those packages need
(see [renv: declaring packages in `DESCRIPTION`](0565-virtual-environments-r-renv-description.qmd)):

```{.yaml}
Type: project
Version: 0.1.0
Description: The R packages this project uses. renv.lock locks them.
Depends:
    cowsay (== 1.2.2)
```

`renv.lock` records R 4.6.2, the repository the packages came from
([Posit Package Manager](https://p3m.dev/)),
and cowsay and the packages it needs.
`.Rprofile` runs `renv/activate.R`, which turns on the project's library when R starts.
On your computer, restore the packages and run the script:

```bash
Rscript -e 'renv::restore(prompt = FALSE)'
Rscript hello.R
```

`renv::restore()` installs the three packages in `renv.lock`, and `hello.R` prints:

```out
 ___________________________ 
< Hello from R in my image! >
 --------------------------- 
      \
       \

        ^__^ 
        (oo)\ ________ 
        (__)\         )\ /\ 
             ||------w|
             ||      ||
```

## A `Dockerfile` for an renv project

Here is the project's `Dockerfile`.
Its renv lines are the same as in [docker-uv-renv](https://github.com/chendaniely/docker-uv-renv),
the example project that [Docker Compose](0650-containers-docker-compose.qmd) uses:

```{.dockerfile}
# Ubuntu with R. Other versions:
# https://rocker-project.org/images/versioned/r-ver.html
FROM rocker/r-ver:4.6.2

# curl: renv downloads packages with it
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install --yes \
    curl

# The project is mounted over /workspace, so the packages go in /opt
WORKDIR /workspace

# R packages in /opt/renv/library
RUN echo "RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY=/opt/renv/library" >> /usr/local/lib/R/etc/Renviron.site
COPY renv.lock .Rprofile ./
COPY renv/activate.R renv/
RUN Rscript -e "renv::restore()"
```

- `FROM rocker/r-ver:4.6.2` starts from Ubuntu Linux with R 4.6.2,
  the version `renv.lock` records
  (see [the `rocker/r-ver` images](https://rocker-project.org/images/versioned/r-ver.html)).
- The `apt-get` line installs `curl`, which renv downloads packages with.
  Without it, the build still works,
  but renv warns `curl does not appear to be installed; downloads will fail.`
- `WORKDIR /workspace` makes `/workspace` the working directory,
  for the rest of the build and for containers that run from the image.
  You will mount your project folder there.
- The `RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY` line tells renv to keep the project's packages
  in `/opt/renv/library`, instead of in `renv/library` inside the project folder
  (see [renv's paths](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/reference/paths.html)).
  It adds the setting to `Renviron.site`,
  a file that [every R session reads when it starts](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/Startup.html),
  so it applies to the build, to `Rscript`, and to R in a running container.
  The section after next shows why the packages go in `/opt`.
- The two `COPY` lines copy the files `renv::restore()` needs, and not the code:
  `renv.lock`, `.Rprofile`, and the `renv/activate.R` that `.Rprofile` runs.
  Editing `hello.R` then never reinstalls the packages
  (see [Building images](0630-containers-building.qmd)).
- `RUN Rscript -e "renv::restore()"` installs the packages in `renv.lock`.
  Starting R in `/workspace` runs `.Rprofile`, which turns on renv first.

build with `--progress=plain` and `--no-cache`

Here is the `renv::restore()` step, without its download progress lines:

```bash
docker build --progress=plain --no-cache --tag docker-renv .
```

renv installed itself first (the "bootstrapping"),
then installed the three packages from `renv.lock`,
as prebuilt Linux binaries from Posit Package Manager.

## Run the project in a container

Mount the project folder at `/workspace`,
and run the script with `Rscript` in place of the image's default command, `R`:

::: {.panel-tabset group="shell"}
## macOS and Linux

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/workspace" docker-renv Rscript hello.R
```

## Windows (Git Bash)

```bash
docker run --rm -v "/$(pwd):/workspace" docker-renv Rscript hello.R
```

## Windows (PowerShell)

```powershell
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/workspace" docker-renv Rscript hello.R
```
:::

```out
 ___________________________ 
< Hello from R in my image! >
 --------------------------- 
      \
       \

        ^__^ 
        (oo)\ ________ 
        (__)\         )\ /\ 
             ||------w|
             ||      ||
```

## Why the packages go in `/opt/renv/library`

R in the container uses the library in `/opt/renv/library`.
renv added the folders for the operating system and R version to the path:

::: {.panel-tabset group="shell"}
## macOS and Linux

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/workspace" docker-renv Rscript -e ".libPaths()"
```

## Windows (Git Bash)

```bash
docker run --rm -v "/$(pwd):/workspace" docker-renv Rscript -e ".libPaths()"
```

## Windows (PowerShell)

```powershell
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/workspace" docker-renv Rscript -e ".libPaths()"
```
:::

```out
[1] "/opt/renv/library/linux-ubuntu-resolute/R-4.6/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu"                   
[2] "/root/.cache/R/renv/sandbox/linux-ubuntu-resolute/R-4.6/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/25ebdc09"
```

The second path is renv's sandbox, which holds only R's own packages,
so that packages installed in R's system library are not used in the project.

As with uv's `.venv`, the mount hides whatever the image had in `/workspace`,
including a `renv/library` folder.
To see what happens, here is the same image built without the `RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY` line,
run with the project folder mounted:

```out
# Bootstrapping renv 1.3.1 ---------------------------------------------------
- Downloading renv ... OK
- Installing renv  ... OK
- None of the packages recorded in the lockfile are currently installed.
- Use `renv::restore()` to restore the project library.
Error in loadNamespace(x) : there is no package called ‘cowsay’
Calls: loadNamespace -> withRestarts -> withOneRestart -> doWithOneRestart
Execution halted
```

renv found no packages in the mounted folder,
installed itself there,
and the script stopped because cowsay was missing.
renv keeps a folder for each operating system in `renv/library`,
so your computer's own packages were left alone,
but a Linux folder appeared next to them on your computer:

```bash
ls renv/library
```

```out
linux-ubuntu-resolute
macos
```

With `RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY=/opt/renv/library`,
the container uses the packages the image installed,
and leaves your computer's `renv` folder alone.
